sections.title: Identification and cultivation
sections.text: The catalogue entry represents Lolium perenne, perennial ryegrass, rather than the entire genus. This tufted Eurasian grass is about 30–100 cm tall and is widely grown for lawns, pasture and erosion control.

sections.title: Stems and spike
sections.text: The stems are erect or ascending and have fibrous roots. The alternate spikelets lie close against the spike axis and are usually awnless. The species can hybridise with Lolium multiflorum.

sections.title: Food use
sections.text: Perennial ryegrass is used as livestock forage, but this entry does not recommend it for human consumption.
